description:
Site 1 of fz-nml.9. Counts are scalar boxes per 1000 steps, as interp/run/build. Kernel.elem's guard `index < tuple_size(tuple)` makes 0/1000/1000, and so does any user guard `k < tuple_size(t)`.

The root is not compare lowering. There are two guard-dispatch joins: jobs/native.rs lower_guard_dispatch (function-clause guards such as Kernel.elem) and native_codegen/receive.rs emit_guard_dispatch (receive guards). The builder fixed both. emit_ordering_cmp_value (receive.rs:1613) already compares Int against Int with a raw icmp. The box comes from emit_guard_dispatch (receive.rs:1456). The join block `done` is created before any outcome body is emitted, and its one I64 param is always an AnyRef (receive.rs:1498). Every Outcome arm therefore runs emit_receive_value_ref, which calls fz_box_int_for_any, even when the body is guard_extern fz_tuple_size returning ReceiveValue::Int. The compare then sees a ref, which is where fz_value_cmp_raw_const comes in.

Fix: emit the outcome bodies first, then decide the join's lane from the values they actually produced. When every value-carrying outcome agrees on one raw lane (Int, Float or Atom), `done` takes that lane and nothing is boxed. When the lanes are mixed, each predecessor converts to a ref before its jump, as happens today. Outcomes that Fail never reach `done`. emit_short_circuit_guard (receive.rs:1559) follows the same rule if it carries a value. There is no static lane predictor; the emitted values decide.

Done when the elem guard and a user `k < tuple_size(t)` guard make 0 scalar boxes on all three paths, pinned by fixture 01702 together with a mixed-lane guard that still answers correctly.

Approved by the user 2026-11-17. The JSON session corrected this site after the builder traced the CLIF (e_param.clif block7: fz_tuple_size -> fz_box_int_for_any -> jump block6).
title: A guard dispatch's result keeps the lane its outcome bodies agree on
